deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This setting controls whether destructive deletion of the service perimeter is prevented. Because preventing deletion protects the perimeter from accidental or unauthorized destruction, it is a security-relevant lifecycle control.

parent.description:
The AccessPolicy this ServicePerimeter lives in.
Format: accessPolicies/{policy_id}
parent.rationale: This field references the parent Access Policy. A generic policy cannot safely restrict environment-specific policy identifiers.

service_perimeters.description: The desired Service Perimeters that should replace all existing Service Perimeters in the Access Policy.

service_perimeters.description.description:
Description of the ServicePerimeter and its use. Does not affect
behavior.
service_perimeters.description.rationale: This field is informational only and does not change the Service Perimeter's access-control behaviour.

service_perimeters.name.rationale: This field identifies the Service Perimeter. A generic policy should not hardcode environment-specific resource names.

service_perimeters.perimeter_type.description:
Specifies the type of the Perimeter. There are two types: regular and
bridge. Regular Service Perimeter contains resources, access levels,
and restricted services. Every resource can be in at most
ONE regular Service Perimeter.

In addition to being in a regular service perimeter, a resource can also
be in zero or more perimeter bridges. A perimeter bridge only contains
resources. Cross project operations are permitted if all effected
resources share some perimeter (whether bridge or regular). Perimeter
Bridge does not contain access levels or services: those are governed
entirely by the regular perimeter that resource is in.

Perimeter Bridges are typically useful when building more complex
topologies with many independent perimeters that need to share some data
with a common perimeter, but should not be able to share data among
themselves. Default value: "PERIMETER_TYPE_REGULAR" Possible values: ["PERIMETER_TYPE_REGULAR", "PERIMETER_TYPE_BRIDGE"]
service_perimeters.perimeter_type.rationale: Defines the functional perimeter type, such as regular or bridge. This is an architectural design choice rather than a platform-level security control.

service_perimeters.title.description: Human readable title. Must be unique within the Policy.
service_perimeters.title.rationale: This field is a human-readable label and does not affect access-control enforcement.

service_perimeters.use_explicit_dry_run_.description:
Use explicit dry run spec flag. Ordinarily, a dry-run spec implicitly exists
for all Service Perimeters, and that spec is identical to the status for those
Service Perimeters. When this flag is set, it inhibits the generation of the
implicit spec, thereby allowing the user to explicitly provide a
configuration ("spec") to use in a dry-run version of the Service Perimeter.
This allows the user to test changes to the enforced config ("status") without
actually enforcing them. This testing is done through analyzing the differences
between currently enforced and suggested restrictions. useExplicitDryRunSpec must
bet set to True if any of the fields in the spec are set to non-default values.
service_perimeters.use_explicit_dry_run_.rationale: Controls whether an explicit dry-run specification is used for testing and validation. This is an operational configuration rather than a platform-level security control.

service_perimeters.spec.description:
Proposed (or dry run) ServicePerimeter configuration.
This configuration allows to specify and test ServicePerimeter configuration
without enforcing actual access restrictions. Only allowed to be set when
the 'useExplicitDryRunSpec' flag is set.

service_perimeters.spec.access_levels.description:
A list of AccessLevel resource names that allow resources within
the ServicePerimeter to be accessed from the internet.
AccessLevels listed must be in the same policy as this
ServicePerimeter. Referencing a nonexistent AccessLevel is a
syntax error. If no AccessLevel names are listed, resources within
the perimeter can only be accessed via GCP calls with request
origins within the perimeter. For Service Perimeter Bridge, must
be empty.

Format: accessPolicies/{policy_id}/accessLevels/{access_level_name}
service_perimeters.spec.access_levels.rationale: References an Access Level resource managed separately by the organisation. The PDE should not constrain team-specific resource references.

service_perimeters.spec.resources.rationale: Contains team-specific resource references. The PDE should not enforce environment-specific resource identifiers.

service_perimeters.spec.restricted_servi.description:
GCP services that are subject to the Service Perimeter
restrictions. Must contain a list of services. For example, if
'storage.googleapis.com' is specified, access to the storage
buckets inside the perimeter must meet the perimeter's access
restrictions.
service_perimeters.spec.restricted_servi.rationale: This argument defines the services protected by the service perimeter. Requiring explicit protected services helps ensure the perimeter has a meaningful boundary instead of leaving service protection empty or overly broad.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies.description:
List of EgressPolicies to apply to the perimeter. A perimeter may
have multiple EgressPolicies, each of which is evaluated separately.
Access is granted if any EgressPolicy grants it. Must be empty for
a perimeter bridge.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..description: Human readable title. Must be unique within the perimeter. Does not affect behavior.
service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..rationale: This field is a human-readable label and does not affect access-control enforcement.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..description: Defines conditions on the source of a request causing this 'EgressPolicy' to apply.

Identities can be an individual user, service account, Google group,
or third-party identity. For third-party identity, only single identities
are supported and other identity types are not supported.The v1 identities
that have the prefix user, group and serviceAccount in
https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/principal-identifiers#v1 are supported.
service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..rationale: This argument defines the identities permitted by an egress rule and therefore controls principal-level data exfiltration pathways. Security policy can constrain overly broad or wildcard identities without hardcoding organisation-specific users or accounts.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..description:
Specifies the type of identities that are allowed access to outside the
perimeter. If left unspecified, then members of 'identities' field will
be allowed access. Possible values: ["IDENTITY_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "ANY_IDENTITY", "ANY_USER_ACCOUNT", "ANY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT"]
service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..rationale: This argument controls the category of identities permitted to egress the perimeter, including broad types such as ANY_IDENTITY, ANY_USER_ACCOUNT, and ANY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT. Enforcing safe identity types helps prevent unrestricted outbound access.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..description: Whether to enforce traffic restrictions based on 'sources' field. If the 'sources' field is non-empty, then this field must be set to 'SOURCE_RESTRICTION_ENABLED'. Possible values: ["SOURCE_RESTRICTION_UNSPECIFIED", "SOURCE_RESTRICTION_ENABLED", "SOURCE_RESTRICTION_DISABLED"]
service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..rationale: This argument controls whether egress traffic is restricted using the configured sources. Requiring an explicit source restriction helps prevent outbound access from being left unrestricted or unspecified.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..description: Sources that this EgressPolicy authorizes access from.
An AccessLevel resource name that allows resources outside the ServicePerimeter to be accessed from the inside.
service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..rationale: References an Access Level resource managed separately by the organisation. The PDE should not constrain team-specific resource references.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..description:
A Google Cloud resource that is allowed to egress the perimeter.
Requests from these resources are allowed to access data outside the perimeter.
Currently only projects are allowed. Project format: 'projects/{project_number}'.
The resource may be in any Google Cloud organization, not just the
organization that the perimeter is defined in. '*' is not allowed, the
case of allowing all Google Cloud resources only is not supported.
service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..rationale: Contains team-specific resource references. The PDE should not enforce environment-specific resource identifiers.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..description:
Defines the conditions on the 'ApiOperation' and destination resources that
cause this 'EgressPolicy' to apply.

A list of external resources that are allowed to be accessed. A request
matches if it contains an external resource in this list (Example:
s3://bucket/path). Currently '*' is not allowed.
service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..rationale: Contains team-specific external destination resource references. The PDE should not enforce environment-specific resource identifiers.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..description:
A list of resources, currently only projects in the form
'projects/<projectnumber>', that match this to stanza. A request matches
if it contains a resource in this list. If * is specified for resources,
then this 'EgressTo' rule will authorize access to all resources outside
the perimeter.
service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..rationale: Contains team-specific resource references. The PDE should not enforce environment-specific resource identifiers.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..description:
A list of IAM roles that represent the set of operations that the sources
specified in the corresponding 'EgressFrom'
are allowed to perform.
service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..rationale: Contains team-specific IAM role assignments. The PDE does not prescribe which IAM roles organisations must use.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..description:
A list of 'ApiOperations' that this egress rule applies to. A request matches
if it contains an operation/service in this list.

The name of the API whose methods or permissions the 'IngressPolicy' or
'EgressPolicy' want to allow. A single 'ApiOperation' with serviceName
field set to '*' will allow all methods AND permissions for all services.
service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..rationale: This argument defines which API service an egress rule may access. Constraining broad or wildcard service names helps prevent overly broad outbound access and reduces potential data-exfiltration channels.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..description:
API methods or permissions to allow. Method or permission must belong
to the service specified by 'serviceName' field. A single MethodSelector
entry with '*' specified for the 'method' field will allow all methods
AND permissions for the service specified in 'serviceName'.

Value for 'method' should be a valid method name for the corresponding
'serviceName' in 'ApiOperation'. If '*' used as value for method,
then ALL methods and permissions are allowed.
service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..rationale: This argument controls the API methods permitted by an egress rule. A wildcard method can allow all methods and permissions for a service, so policy should prevent overly broad wildcard access.

service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..description:
Value for permission should be a valid Cloud IAM permission for the
corresponding 'serviceName' in 'ApiOperation'.
service_perimeters.spec.egress_policies..rationale: This argument controls granular IAM permissions allowed by an egress rule. It is security relevant because policy can prevent wildcard or overly permissive selections without prescribing organisation-specific custom permissions.

service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.description:
List of 'IngressPolicies' to apply to the perimeter. A perimeter may
have multiple 'IngressPolicies', each of which is evaluated
separately. Access is granted if any 'Ingress Policy' grants it.
Must be empty for a perimeter bridge.
Human readable title. Must be unique within the perimeter. Does not affect behavior.
service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.rationale: This field is a human-readable label and does not affect access-control enforcement.

service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.description:
Defines the conditions on the source of a request causing this 'IngressPolicy'
to apply.

A list of identities that are allowed access through this ingress policy.
Should be in the format of email address. The email address should represent
individual user or service account only.
service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.rationale: This argument defines the identities allowed to enter the service perimeter. Security policy can block public or overly broad principals and wildcard-style identity exposure to preserve the perimeter boundary.

service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.description:
Specifies the type of identities that are allowed access from outside the
perimeter. If left unspecified, then members of 'identities' field will be
allowed access. Possible values: ["IDENTITY_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "ANY_IDENTITY", "ANY_USER_ACCOUNT", "ANY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT"]
service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.rationale: This argument controls broad categories of identities allowed to enter the perimeter, including ANY_IDENTITY. Enforcing safe identity types helps prevent unrestricted principal access across the perimeter boundary.

service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.description: Sources that this 'IngressPolicy' authorizes access from.

An 'AccessLevel' resource name that allow resources within the
'ServicePerimeters' to be accessed from the internet. 'AccessLevels' listed
must be in the same policy as this 'ServicePerimeter'. Referencing a nonexistent
'AccessLevel' will cause an error. If no 'AccessLevel' names are listed,
resources within the perimeter can only be accessed via Google Cloud calls
with request origins within the perimeter.
Example 'accessPolicies/MY_POLICY/accessLevels/MY_LEVEL.'
If * is specified, then all IngressSources will be allowed.
service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.rationale: References an Access Level resource managed separately by the organisation. The PDE should not constrain team-specific resource references.

service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.description:
A Google Cloud resource that is allowed to ingress the perimeter.
Requests from these resources will be allowed to access perimeter data.
Currently only projects are allowed. Format 'projects/{project_number}'
The project may be in any Google Cloud organization, not just the
organization that the perimeter is defined in. '*' is not allowed, the case
of allowing all Google Cloud resources only is not supported.
service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.rationale: Contains team-specific resource references. The PDE should not enforce environment-specific resource identifiers.

service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.description:
Defines the conditions on the 'ApiOperation' and request destination that cause
this 'IngressPolicy' to apply.

A list of resources, currently only projects in the form
'projects/<projectnumber>', protected by this 'ServicePerimeter'
that are allowed to be accessed by sources defined in the
corresponding 'IngressFrom'. A request matches if it contains
a resource in this list. If '*' is specified for resources,
then this 'IngressTo' rule will authorize access to all
resources inside the perimeter, provided that the request
also matches the 'operations' field.
service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.rationale: Contains team-specific resource references. The PDE should not enforce environment-specific resource identifiers.

service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.description:
A list of IAM roles that represent the set of operations that the sources
specified in the corresponding 'IngressFrom'
are allowed to perform.
service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.rationale: Contains team-specific IAM role assignments. The PDE does not prescribe which IAM roles organisations must use.

service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.description:
A list of 'ApiOperations' the sources specified in corresponding 'IngressFrom'
are allowed to perform in this 'ServicePerimeter'.

The name of the API whose methods or permissions the 'IngressPolicy' or
'EgressPolicy' want to allow. A single 'ApiOperation' with 'serviceName'
field set to '*' will allow all methods AND permissions for all services.
service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.rationale: This argument defines which API service may be reached through an ingress rule. Constraining broad or wildcard service names ensures inbound access is explicitly scoped to approved services.

service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.description:
API methods or permissions to allow. Method or permission must belong to
the service specified by serviceName field. A single 'MethodSelector' entry
with '*' specified for the method field will allow all methods AND
permissions for the service specified in 'serviceName'.

Value for method should be a valid method name for the corresponding
serviceName in 'ApiOperation'. If '*' used as value for 'method', then
ALL methods and permissions are allowed.
service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.rationale: This argument names a specific API method used by the workload. Method selection is fine-grained operational configuration rather than a generic platform-level security control.

service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.description:
Value for permission should be a valid Cloud IAM permission for the
corresponding 'serviceName' in 'ApiOperation'.
service_perimeters.spec.ingress_policies.rationale: This argument names a specific API permission required by the workload. Permission selection is functional, team-specific configuration rather than a generic platform-level security control.

service_perimeters.spec.vpc_accessible_s.description:
Specifies how APIs are allowed to communicate within the Service
Perimeter.

The list of APIs usable within the Service Perimeter.
Must be empty unless 'enableRestriction' is True.
service_perimeters.spec.vpc_accessible_s.rationale: This argument is an allowlist of APIs usable within the service perimeter. Restricting the allowed services helps prevent unauthorized service access and reduces data-exfiltration exposure.

service_perimeters.spec.vpc_accessible_s.description:
Whether to restrict API calls within the Service Perimeter to the
list of APIs specified in 'allowedServices'.
service_perimeters.spec.vpc_accessible_s.rationale: This flag enables VPC accessibility restrictions for APIs inside the service perimeter. Enforcing the restriction is a security feature that limits service exposure to the configured allowlist.

service_perimeters.status.description:
ServicePerimeter configuration. Specifies sets of resources,
restricted services and access levels that determine
perimeter content and boundaries.

service_perimeters.status.access_levels.description:
A list of AccessLevel resource names that allow resources within
the ServicePerimeter to be accessed from the internet.
AccessLevels listed must be in the same policy as this
ServicePerimeter. Referencing a nonexistent AccessLevel is a
syntax error. If no AccessLevel names are listed, resources within
the perimeter can only be accessed via GCP calls with request
origins within the perimeter. For Service Perimeter Bridge, must
be empty.

Format: accessPolicies/{policy_id}/accessLevels/{access_level_name}
service_perimeters.status.access_levels.rationale: This is a status field representing the applied Service Perimeter configuration rather than a generic platform security control.

service_perimeters.status.resources.rationale: This is a status field representing the applied Service Perimeter configuration rather than a generic platform security control.

service_perimeters.status.restricted_ser.description:
GCP services that are subject to the Service Perimeter
restrictions. Must contain a list of services. For example, if

buckets inside the perimeter must meet the perimeter's access
restrictions.
service_perimeters.status.restricted_ser.rationale: This is a status field representing the applied Service Perimeter configuration rather than a generic platform security control.

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.description:
List of EgressPolicies to apply to the perimeter. A perimeter may
have multiple EgressPolicies, each of which is evaluated separately.
Access is granted if any EgressPolicy grants it. Must be empty for
a perimeter bridge.
Human readable title. Must be unique within the perimeter. Does not affect behavior.
service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.rationale: This field is a human-readable label and does not affect access-control enforcement.

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.description: Defines conditions on the source of a request causing this 'EgressPolicy' to apply.

A list of identities that are allowed access through this 'EgressPolicy'.
Should be in the format of email address. The email address should
represent individual user or service account only.
service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.rationale: This is a status field representing the applied Service Perimeter configuration rather than a generic platform security control.

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.description:
Specifies the type of identities that are allowed access to outside the
perimeter. If left unspecified, then members of 'identities' field will
be allowed access. Possible values: ["IDENTITY_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "ANY_IDENTITY", "ANY_USER_ACCOUNT", "ANY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT"]
service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.rationale: This configuration controls the category of identities permitted to egress the perimeter. Broad identity types can weaken the boundary, so constraining them is a security-relevant control against unrestricted outbound access.

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.description: Whether to enforce traffic restrictions based on 'sources' field. If the 'sources' field is non-empty, then this field must be set to 'SOURCE_RESTRICTION_ENABLED'. Possible values: ["SOURCE_RESTRICTION_UNSPECIFIED", "SOURCE_RESTRICTION_ENABLED", "SOURCE_RESTRICTION_DISABLED"]
service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.rationale: This configuration governs whether egress traffic is restricted by the configured sources. Enforcing explicit source restrictions helps prevent unrestricted outbound flows from the service perimeter.

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.description: Sources that this EgressPolicy authorizes access from.
An AccessLevel resource name that allows resources outside the ServicePerimeter to be accessed from the inside.
service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.rationale: This argument references an Access Level resource. Because it is a pointer to another team-managed resource, a generic platform policy should not constrain the specific reference.

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.description:
A Google Cloud resource that is allowed to egress the perimeter.

The resource may be in any Google Cloud organization, not just the
organization that the perimeter is defined in. '*' is not allowed, the

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.rationale: This argument identifies a specific source resource. Resource identifiers are team-specific architectural references and are not appropriate generic platform policy targets.

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.description:
A list of resources, currently only projects in the form

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.rationale: This argument references specific destination resources. Resource identifiers are team-specific architectural choices and should not be constrained by a generic platform policy.

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.description:

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.description:
A list of 'ApiOperations' that this egress rule applies to. A request matches

The name of the API whose methods or permissions the 'IngressPolicy' or

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.rationale: This argument identifies the target API service for an egress rule. The service name is an architectural reference rather than a generic structural security control.

service_perimeters.status.egress_policie.description:

Value for permission should be a valid Cloud IAM permission for the

service_perimeters.status.ingress_polici.rationale: This argument names a specific API permission required by the workload. Permission identifiers are workload-specific and are not appropriate targets for a generic platform policy.

service_perimeters.status.vpc_accessible.description:
Specifies how APIs are allowed to communicate within the Service
Perimeter.

The list of APIs usable within the Service Perimeter.
Must be empty unless 'enableRestriction' is True.
service_perimeters.status.vpc_accessible.rationale: This argument defines the list of APIs usable within the service perimeter when VPC accessibility restriction is enabled. The specific allowed-service list is organisation and workload dependent, so a generic PDE policy should not pin a fixed service list.

service_perimeters.status.vpc_accessible.description:
Whether to restrict API calls within the Service Perimeter to the
list of APIs specified in 'allowedServices'.
service_perimeters.status.vpc_accessible.rationale: This flag enables VPC accessibility restrictions for APIs within the service perimeter. Enforcing the restriction is a core perimeter-security feature that limits API exposure.
